To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we design and implement EagleEye, a wearable camera based AR system that identifies missing people in crowded urban spaces, and that it is 9.07 times faster than naive execution with only 108KBytes of data offload.

we present EagleEye, a wearable camera system for person identification in large, crowded spaces, which achieves high accuracy and low latency using novel techniques for face identification and parallel DNN pipeline execution on mobile and cloud.
we present a wearable AR based system, EagleEye, that identifies missing person or people in large, crowded, urban spaces.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a wearable camera based system that can help identify missing person (or persons) in crowded urban spaces in real-time.
the design of a system for missing person identification in large, urban, and crowded spaces.
the development and evaluation of a novel AR based system for missing person identification in large urban environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our system is the first to enable accurate person identification in a large, crowded urban environment, with a latency that is suitable for a mobile application.
we propose EagleEye, a novel system that enables accurate identification of people in crowded urban spaces.
EagleEye enables the identification of a missing person in a crowd in real-time, with a high degree of accuracy and low latency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a novel wearable system that can accurately identify people from LR face images in real-time and in crowded urban spaces with low latency.
we present a novel system that can accurately identify people in large, crowded spaces.

we design a novel face identification pipeline to accurately identify LR faces in crowded urban environments and develop a novel parallelization technique to efficiently execute the pipeline on mobile devices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
EagleEye is the first AR system that can accurately and efficiently identify a person in a crowded urban space, and we hope it will inspire future AR systems for other challenging tasks.

we demonstrate that it is possible to run complex multi DNN based face identification pipeline in real time on mobile devices, and that this enables novel AR based systems that can be deployed in real world settings.
EagleEye demonstrates that it is possible to design a real-time, accurate, and privacy preserving AR based system for missing person identification in large, crowded public spaces.
